newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador oil workers plan action against minister.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador oil workers plan action against minister.

text.p: Union leaders at Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador announced a protest campaign Friday against insults they say were flung at them by Energy Minister Alfredo Adum and his plans to sell off parts of the firm.

Union boss Ivan Narvaez said Petroecuador workers would stage marches and debates and paralyze administration and maintenance operations from October 10 until they get "a political trial and the sacking of minister Adum."
Government officials including President Abdala Bucaram accused Petroecuador workers last week of being involved in stealing petrol and defending unjustified work privileges.

Adum is engaged in a legal battle with petrol workers' leader and congressman Marcelo Roman, of the Pachacutik indigenous party. The minister is suing Roman for libel and Roman is suing the minister for verbal abuse.

"We petrol workers have never meant harm to Ecuadorans but this time things have gone too far," said Narvaez. "You can't call 4,000 professionals who generate 52 percent of the budget delinquents, mafiosi, thieves and sons of bitches."
